summary: Gradual throughput erosion in reserved pool during rolling small-tenant burst cohort
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (ClearWrite Inc.) reports gradual degradation of p50/p95 throughput for their reserved capacity pool over a 3-hour window during midday. Impact is sustained increased latency for short streaming requests and lower token throughput for batched routes.

Impact:
- ClearWrite reports ~30% drop in observed tokens/sec and p95 latency increase from 120ms -> 380ms on their primary routes.
- No full outage; requests succeed but user-facing processing time degrades.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-03-10 14:05: ClearWrite alerted via support email about rising latency.
- 2026-03-10 14:12: Support triaged, customer provided sample request IDs and timestamps.
- 2026-03-10 14:25: SRE cursory check shows reserved pool attach latency rising and more frequent NVLink stalls.
- 2026-03-10 15:40: Autoscaler did not trigger extra nodes; allocation credits dipped but no hard OOMs.
- 2026-03-10 16:20: We observed periodic small-tenant bursts (many short streams) correlated to slot fragmentation.

Environment:
- Dedicated reserved pool (tenant_id: cw-prod-01) in us-west running a mix of streaming and batched routes.
- Model variants: open_llama_7b-v2 (fp16 path) and velvet-3B-quant (quantized).

Observed behavior / metrics:
- GPU attach latency p50 increased from 12ms -> 85ms across pool during window.
- p99 kernel queue wait increased and batcher serialization events rose ~3x.
- Autoscaler telemetry shows brief credit starvation events with no sustained scale-up (allocations fluctuated but no new nodes).
- KV cache hit rate remained stable; prefetch queue length increased for short streams.

Why this is surprising:
- Reserved capacity should absorb short spikes; autoscaler should react to credit dips. Instead we see slot fragmentation and slow attach without scale-up, consistent with many small concurrent short-lived streams (noisy cohort) that prevent efficient batching and GPU slot reuse.

Hypothesis:
- A cohort of ephemeral short-stream tenants created a burst fan-out pattern that fragments slot allocation and increases attach syscall rates, leading to transient NVLink/io contention and autoscaler misreading the signal as recoverable (no policy scale-up).

Next steps planned:
- Instrument per-tenant short-stream rate and slot hold time.
- Temporarily apply soft rate-limiter and connection coalescing for identified noisy tenant cohort.
- Tune autoscaler sensitivity for short-stream bursts (lower threshold for scale-up on repeated attach latency spikes).
- Run controlled repro (see steps_to_reproduce) in staging with synthetic short-stream cohort.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) In a staging reserved pool, start 200 ephemeral short streaming connections across 20 tenants with mean request length 20 tokens and inter-arrival 50-200ms.
2) Simultaneously run normal batched routes at steady rate for the target tenant.
3) Observe slot allocation churn, attach latency, and autoscaler telemetry for 30+ minutes.
4) Compare batcher serialization rate and NVLink utilization against baseline.
observed_metrics: gpu_attach_p50: 12ms -> 85ms; batcher_serialize_events: x1 -> x3; tokens_per_sec(customer): -30%; autoscaler_allocation_attempts: unchanged with short credit dips; nvlink_io_wait: +40% (sampled)
hypothesis: Transient multi-tenant short-stream fanout causing slot fragmentation and NVLink/io contention; autoscaler hysteresis prevents timely scale-up because metrics appear ephemeral.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 14:30 - SRE (Marco Ruiz): correlated request IDs to pool attach spikes; found clusters of short connections from 18 tenants with >80% short-stream traffic.
2026-03-10 15:05 - Support (Aisha Patel): requested connection logs and client SDK versions from ClearWrite; they use SDK v2.1.3 with default keepalive=30s.

2026-03-10 15:40 - SRE: observed autoscaler metric smoothing window is 5m; attach spikes lasted 2-6m and were below scale threshold; proposing config change to 90s smoothing for attach-latency alerts.
2026-03-10 16:10 - Eng (Jin Park): Kernel queue traces show increased enqueue/dequeue latency consistent with small-batch thrash and increased PCIe doorbell latency.
2026-03-11 09:00 - SRE: replayed a 20-minute sample in staging and validated slot fragmentation reproduction using the short-stream generator.
workaround: Applied tenant-level soft rate limit for the identified noisy cohort (internal policy id: softrl-2026-03-cw01) and enabled connection coalescing on sidecar for 1h window; observed immediate partial recovery in customer tokens/sec (+15%).
resolution: Mitigation in progress. Short-term mitigation (soft rate limit + coalescing) applied. Engineering to propose autoscaler smoothing policy change and add short-stream detection heuristic. Patch PR opened for autoscaler: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/512 (referenced). Plan to follow with a formal rollout after validation in staging.
postmortem_followup_items: Add short-stream cohort detection metric and per-tenant short-stream rate dashboards (owner: SRE)
Adjust autoscaler smoothing and sensitivity for attach-latency spikes triggered by short bursts (owner: infra-eng)
Improve SDK connection coalescing docs and recommend keepalive tuning for dedicated pools (owner: developer-experience)
Add automated canary to detect slot fragmentation during reserved pool load tests (owner: test-automation)
Communicate workaround and recommended client config to ClearWrite and schedule follow-up call (owner: CS)
